name: build-test-review
description: Implement, verify with an independent QA worker, then an independent code review; deliver only when both pass.
when: A task that changes behavior or code in a project, whose requirements are clear enough to implement without a written plan first, and that warrants independent verification and review before delivery. Not for tiny or mechanical work (use the chore role, no workflow), not for an unclear or oversized request (plan-build-test-review), and not when no-mistakes is the selected delivery path, which owns review and testing itself.

qa-fix.description: QA failed or gave feedback: the implementer fixes it, then QA evaluates again against that feedback.

review-fix.description: Code review gave feedback: the implementer fixes it, the orchestrator decides whether QA must run again, then the review is repeated on the corrected delta.

implement.instruction: Implement the task. Verify it by running it, commit the work to the task branch, and report the commit range of your change. If a feedback input is present it is QA's findings on your previous change: address every item by id - fix it, or say concretely why it does not apply - and report on each id.

qa.instruction: Verify the change independently against the task's acceptance, by running it and probing the behavior the task implies beyond the implementer's own checks. Do not edit the change. If a feedback input is present it is the previous findings that the change was corrected for: first report on each id (fixed or still failing, with what you ran), then evaluate the whole change again.

review.instruction: Review the change for correctness first, then maintainability and safety. QA has already run the change, so spend your attention on what a test run does not show. If a feedback input is present it is your previous findings and the change is the corrected delta: confirm each id is fixed or still open, then review the delta itself.

address-review.instruction: The code review found problems in your change. Address every feedback item by id - fix it, or say concretely why it does not apply - verify, commit to the task branch, and report the commit range of the corrected change together with what each id needed.

requalify.question: Does the change made in response to the review feedback require QA to run again before the review is repeated?
criteria: yes (QA again, then review): the fix changed behavior, logic, data handling, an interface, a test, a dependency or configuration - anything a test run could now see differently - or it is more than a trivial edit, or the finding it answers was about correctness or safety.

no (review the delta directly): the fix is limited to naming, comments, formatting, documentation or removal of dead code with no behavioral effect, and the implementer reports the project's own checks still pass.
When in doubt, yes. Record the reason; it is kept in the workflow state.

deliver.instruction: QA and code review both passed. Deliver through the task's own delivery mode: for direct-PR the worker that owns the branch pushes it and opens the PR ready for review. Never merge: merging stays the captain's word.
